_VALCOLS = [_c for _c in EXPORT_COLS if not _c.startswith("FLAG_")]

assert list(_written.columns) == EXPORT_COLS, "unexpected columns in the written file"
assert len(_written) == len(export_df), "record count changed on write"
assert _written.index.equals(export_df.index), "index changed on write"
for _c in EXPORT_COLS:
    assert int(_written[_c].notna().sum()) == int(export_df[_c].notna().sum()), \
        f"{_c}: non-null count changed on write - gaps may have become zeros"
for _c in _FLAGCOLS:
    assert _written[_c].equals(export_df[_c]), f"{_c} changed on write"
for _c in _VALCOLS:
    assert abs(float(_written[_c].sum()) - float(export_df[_c].sum())) < 1e-6, \
        f"{_c}: values changed on write"

What is in the exported file

The manifest, read back from disk rather than taken from the frame in memory.

import matplotlib.dates as mdates

KIND_STYLE = {
    "individual": ("#90A4AE", "individual channel, as measured (raw)"),
    "overall": ("#00897B", "overall column, gap-filled"),
    "method flag": ("#FB8C00", "method (bar = a value is present)"),
    "suspect flag": ("#D32F2F", "suspect (bar = flag == 1)"),
}


def column_kind(c: str) -> str:
    if c.endswith("_METHOD"):
        return "method flag"
    if c.endswith("_SUSPECT"):
        return "suspect flag"
    if c.endswith("_HOMOGENIZED_GAPFILLED"):
        return "overall"
    return "individual"


def carries_information(frame: pd.DataFrame, c: str) -> pd.Series:
    """Where a column says something. Not `notna()` for a flag: a flag is defined at every record,
    so notna() would report 100 % for all of them and hide exactly what the reader wants to see."""
    _k = column_kind(c)
    if _k in ("individual", "overall"):
        return frame[c].notna()
    return frame[c] != 0 if _k == "method flag" else frame[c] == 1


def _depth_of_col(c):
    # The depth token, robust to the extra segment in TS_PRF_FF1_<d>_1: the first _<number>_ or
    # _<number>-at-end that matches one of this profile's depths.
    return next(float(d) for d in DEPTHS if re.search(rf"_{re.escape(d)}(?:_|$)", c))


_rows = []
for _c in EXPORT_COLS:
    _k = column_kind(_c)
    _av = carries_information(_written, _c)
    _rows.append({"column": _c, "kind": _k, "depth_m": _depth_of_col(_c),
                  "unit": "degC" if _k in ("individual", "overall") else "code",
                  "n": int(_av.sum()), "coverage_%": round(100 * float(_av.mean()), 1),
                  "first": _av.index[_av][0] if _av.any() else pd.NaT,
                  "last": _av.index[_av][-1] if _av.any() else pd.NaT})
MANIFEST = pd.DataFrame(_rows).set_index("column")
print("Table: the manifest of the written file: every column, its kind, unit, coverage and span, "
      "read back from disk rather than taken from memory")
display(MANIFEST)

# The figure doubles as a check: the method flag must carry a value code in exactly the records
# where the overall column has a value.
for _d in DEPTHS:
    assert MANIFEST.loc[methodcol(_d), "n"] == MANIFEST.loc[homogcol(_d), "n"], \
        f"{methodcol(_d)} is non-zero in a different number of records than {homogcol(_d)} has values"
print("Every method-flag row matches its overall column exactly.")

⚠️ Notes for downstream users

Columns

  • Two kinds per depth. The individual channels (TS_FF1_0.05_1, _2, _3, _4, TS_PRF_FF1_0.05_1, …) are the raw measurements, one sensor each, gaps where that sensor was down. The overall column TS_FF1_<d>_HOMOGENIZED_GAPFILLED reconciles a depth’s sensors into one gap-filled series. Use the first for the truth of one instrument, the second for a single number per depth.
  • Filter on FLAG_…_METHOD. 1 measured (modern), 2 measured (early), 3 modelled with the nearest contributing depth ≤ 0.15 m away, 4 modelled with the nearest one further off, 0 no value. For measured-only keep METHOD ∈ {1, 2}.
  • 3 and 4 are provenance, not a quality ranking. They record how far the nearest contributing depth was, and since the fill uses every available depth at once, a 4 is not necessarily worse than a 3: held out on the deep-hole case the errors are 0.17 K at 0.2 m and 0.26 K at 0.3 m (both 3) against 0.22 K at 0.5 m and 0.26 K at 0.6 m (both 4). Earlier versions of this product described 4 as “the weakest estimates, safe to drop”; that is no longer true, and blanket-excluding 4 now discards the 0.5 m fill, which is among the best modelled values in the file.
  • Values are °C. The modern record sits on a 0.1 K grid, which matters below 0.3 m: the median summer daily amplitude at 0.5 m and 0.6 m is one grid step, so a diurnal cycle in the deep columns is quantisation, not soil.
  • Depths are not replicates. They share a logger, a power supply and an SDI-12 bus, so they fail together, but they do not measure the same soil and their disagreement is information.

Two dates that do not affect this product

  • The January 2016 site renewal did not reach this profile, although it moved TA by 1.32 °C, stepped RH and PA, and broke much of LW_IN that June. The renewal replaced the tower installation; this station is on the forest-floor logger, the tower program takes no soil temperature, no records were lost while the tower logger was replaced, and no half-hour in the surrounding three weeks exceeds the record’s own routine scatter. The level test that could see a change common to every channel resolves about ±0.75 K, and within that nothing happens — a null stated with its resolution rather than as a bare claim.
  • The forest-floor rewiring of 25 June 2015 left soil temperature untouched. 09 measures a −3.9 % VWC step in soil moisture at that half-hour. Here the departure sits at the middle of the distribution of the same statistic on comparable mornings at every channel, while 09‘s soil moisture sits in the extreme tail of its own. The event was confined to the soil-moisture chain, which is what the maintenance record implies when it reports the soil-moisture probes’ connectors loose three weeks earlier. Nothing is corrected here, and the comparison is the evidence 09’s attribution rests on.

The gap-fill

  • The overall columns are filled from the other depths of the same profile, by an ordinary least squares fitted separately for each sensor generation (so a fill never introduces a sensor step) over every available depth plus its thermal memory (rolling means from 3 h to 120 d) and a day-of-year harmonic. Validated by leave-one-year-out and by predicting the deep depths from the shallow ones alone. The two-year and the ten-year 0.3/0.5 m gaps are filled, not measured. The individual columns are never filled.
  • The fill changed in notebook version 2 (23 Jul 2026), and the numbers moved a lot. Before it, a missing depth was predicted from the single nearest available depth; now it is predicted from all of them at once, with thermal memory. Held out on the deep-hole case the error fell from 0.55 K to 0.22 K at 0.5 m and from 0.66 K to 0.26 K at 0.6 m, and no depth got worse on either test. The method was chosen by a documented experiment, TS_FF1_GAPFILL_ML_COMPARISON.ipynb, which also rejected boosted trees for this use. If you are comparing against a file produced by version 1, the modelled values differ; the measured ones do not.
  • It interpolates, it does not extrapolate. Each overall column is filled only within that depth’s own measured span, so 0.2 and 0.6 m have no values before 2020 and 0.15 m none after March 2021. Inside a span the only gaps left are the whole-station outages, every depth dead at once (~6 %, the same timestamps in every depth).

Comparing across eras

  • Cross-era homogenisation is measured only at 0.05 and 0.1 m, on the 348-day overlap of the two generations. At 0.3/0.5/0.15 m the eras do not overlap, so the early era sits at its own level (method 2) and a trend across April 2020 there still carries the sensor change. 09’s soil moisture had to homogenise on climatology; that is refused here where it cannot be measured.
  • Do not compute a diurnal or seasonal amplitude across April 2020. The early sensors were better coupled to the surface than today’s at the same nominal depth: at 0.05 m the early daily amplitude is ~3.1 K against ~0.9 K modern. Levels are reconciled, amplitudes are not.
  • Between January 2009 and May 2012 the early profile does not agree with itself. FLAG_…_SUSPECT = 1 marks 0.05, 0.1 and 0.15 m there, including values modelled from the early era. The three channels depart from their own seasonal norm by 1.5-3.5 K in mirror-image pairs; across the other thirteen years they agree to a few tenths of a kelvin. Which of the three is wrong is not determined, so filter on this flag before using the early era quantitatively.
  • The 0.3 m record crosses two probes, and the swap is invisible in the values. The original TEROS 12 fell silent on 2024-04-09; its replacement went in on 2025-03-04, 40 cm down the slope. The dead 328 days are covered by the depth’s other channel, and the replacement reads the same as the original relative to its neighbour, unlike soil moisture, where 09 measures a real +3 % VWC step at the same swap. Flag 5 marks it anyway.

Provenance

  • The early era was screened once, by the MeteoScreeningTool, and never re-screened. The thirteen 20_SCREENING/TS/ notebooks cover the modern channels only. This notebook checks the early era for physical consistency but cannot re-screen it.
  • Ten early field names were dropped as duplicates and three as mislabelled. TS_PRF_FF1_*_2/_3 are the modern profile re-screened by the old tool under a shifted replicate index; TS_FF1_0.05_1/_2/_3 in the mst era are early hardware at an effective 0.15-0.31 m, not 0.05 m. Both exclusions are re-derived on every run, so going back to the raw database, do not read those names as what they are called.
  • There is no 1.0 m or 1.5 m depth, although the database has fields for them: the only records are a two-year block carrying 1,559 values of exactly 0.00 °C and excursions to 211 °C, which nothing has screened.
  • The site record for 2006-2011 is invisible to a date filter. It was pasted into GIN as a single row dated 2011-06-03, so a notebook filtering on Date concludes those years are undocumented. They are not, and two of this product’s four long early gaps are named there to the day. 2004 and 2005 have no site record at all, so statements about the first two years rest on physical evidence alone.

Still open

  • What the early profile physically was — largely settled, by the logger programs. Both surviving forest-floor programs take eight Campbell 107 readings: a five-sensor stick their own location table names SoilT_05/_10/_15/_30/_50, which is exactly this product’s five early depths in the same order, plus separate probes SoilT_A/B/C/D placed with the soil heat-flux plates. So the fieldbook’s three device numbers (773/774/775, trashed 2021-03-25, “replaced by new one (109)”) are not the station’s whole 107 inventory, and the arithmetic that looked wrong — three 107s replaced by two 109s — was never a constraint. The three excluded mst-era TS_FF1_0.05_* channels, at effective 0.15/0.22/0.31 m, are what plate probes look like, the same explanation this notebook already accepts for the modern 109s. What is still open is narrow: which field name is which physical sensor, since nothing ties a device number or a program location to a database field name.
  • Why the early 0.05 m channel is so much livelier than today’s. A shallower installation, a thinner litter layer in 2004, or a different pit; the data cannot separate them. The modern profile shows the same effect in miniature and there the cause is known: the two Campbell 109s went in beside the soil heat-flux plates rather than into the profile pit, and TS_FF1_0.05_4 carries a site entry of its own, “too close to the surface? Very strong daily cycle”.
  • The August 2012 logger clock error. 01-05 shift one block by +15.5 h. That is a tower logger fault, and 09 established that the forest floor is a separate logger whose 2012 fieldbook entry describes a different lag. Soil temperature does have a diurnal cycle at 0.05 m, so unlike soil moisture the fault would in principle be detectable, but only in the early era, where there is no second independent soil sensor to align against. Nothing is applied here.
  • What the 2012-04-25 program did. The entry reads “new Loggerprogramm with corrected multipliers and offset” and names no channels. The programs bound it from one side: in the 2004 and 2006 forest-floor programs every Campbell 107 reading uses Mult 1.0 and Offset 0.0, because the Temp (107) instruction applies Campbell’s polynomial internally, so there was no site-applied soil-temperature scaling to correct. What the 2012 program actually changed cannot be read: no forest-floor program between May 2006 and the modern era survives on disk.
  • Which early channel is wrong between 2009 and 2012, and why. Three explanations fit the timing and the data cannot separate them: a changed multiplier on one channel (the 2012-04-25 entry, which names none), physical disturbance of one sensor during the repeated logger repairs of 2009-2011, or a genuinely drifting probe. A fourth soil sensor from that era would settle it, and none exists.
  • The two-year 2017-2018 block. Excluded as unscreened, but it is the only 0.2 m, 1.0 m and 1.5 m record the site ever produced. Screening it would extend the product downwards, and that is a 20_SCREENING/ job.

End of notebook.

_h, _rem = divmod(int((NOTEBOOK_END - NOTEBOOK_START).total_seconds()), 3600)
_m, _s = divmod(_rem, 60)

print(f"Finished: {NOTEBOOK_END.strftime('%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S')}")
print(f"Runtime:  {_h:02d}:{_m:02d}:{_s:02d} (hh:mm:ss)")
